algorithm.title: Initial management of systemic lupus erythematosus

cell.label: Is the disease clinically unstable, or does it appear to have life-threatening complications?
Do the following organ systems have normal and stable function: renal, skin, joints, hematologic, pulmonary, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, central nervous system?
Are the therapies being considered associated with significant toxicity?
General treatment: patient education; analgesics as needed; NSAIDs as needed; topical steroids for rash; topical sunscreens (minimum sun protection factor 15).

If the patient has diminished quality of life (constitutional symptoms, inadequate analgesia, etc.), consider an antimalarial (eg, hydroxychloroquine 200-400 mg/day) or low-dose corticosteroid (not to exceed 10 mg/day prednisone or equivalent).
